invocation: /ski dog My eight-year-old dog freezes and growls when I touch his hips and I need a grooming plan.
scope: Forward-test preliminary case triage and staged grooming plan; no literature search, images or monograph requested.

interpretation.observation: Freezing and growling occur during hip contact.
possibilities: fear or learned concern about handling
a combination of physical and emotional factors
interpretation.uncertainty: The report does not distinguish these possibilities; age alone does not establish a diagnosis.

preliminary_response: Pause hip touching and grooming that triggers freezing or growling. Give him space to leave, and do not punish growling or keep handling him to test his tolerance. Arrange a veterinary assessment before practising contact with the hips; explain the response before the appointment so the team can plan handling. For grooming that cannot wait, ask the veterinary team for a safe care plan. After medical assessment, build voluntary participation in small, comfortable steps with rewards and stop at the first sign of tension or withdrawal. To tailor this, I need onset, mobility/health changes, bite history, what grooming is essential, and which tools, rewards and positions he tolerates.

required_inputs.question: When did this start, and does it happen only at the hips or with other touch, tools or people?
Any stiffness, difficulty rising/walking, health conditions, sensory changes, recent injury, veterinary findings or current treatment?
Has he snapped, lunged, bitten or made tooth contact, and what happened immediately before and after? Do not recreate the event.
What grooming is needed now, where are any mats or hygiene problems, and can those tasks safely wait?
Who handles him, are children or other animals nearby, and where can he leave and rest undisturbed?
Which resting/standing positions, brushes, sounds and approaches does he already tolerate voluntarily, and what rewards does he enjoy?
What time, space, help and access to a veterinary team or qualified reward-based behavior professional are available?

plan.category: essential; professional support for pain or bite risk
plan.purpose: Meet grooming needs while protecting comfort, choice and warning signals.
prerequisites: Veterinary assessment and individualized handling advice before hip-contact exercises.
Clarify bite history and urgent grooming needs.
Identify a comfortable position, escape route and suitable rewards.
plan.observable_baseline: Hip touch currently produces freezing and growling; other handling tolerance is unknown. Do not repeat the trigger to establish a baseline.
plan.success_criteria: Dog voluntarily participates with loose comfortable movement and can withdraw; grooming is completed only within the veterinary handling plan and observed tolerance. No fixed deadline.
plan.environment: Quiet, non-slip space with room to retreat; keep children and other animals away from practice.
equipment: owner-approved comfortable grooming tool once tolerance is established
reward delivery appropriate to veterinary advice

sequential_steps.action: Pause triggering hip handling; arrange veterinary assessment and triage any grooming that cannot wait.
sequential_steps.gate: Medical and safety needs are addressed before contact training.

sequential_steps.action: After veterinary guidance, reward voluntary approach to a comfortable grooming station or mat. Accept standing or lying as comfortable; do not require a sit.
sequential_steps.gate: Dog chooses to approach and can leave freely.

sequential_steps.action: Introduce the stationary tool at a comfortable distance, pairing its presence with rewards; do not touch the sensitive area.
sequential_steps.gate: Dog remains comfortable and voluntarily re-engages.

sequential_steps.action: With veterinary clearance, introduce one very small handling step at an already comfortable body area, then release and reward.
sequential_steps.gate: No freezing, growling, tension or withdrawal; participation remains voluntary.

sequential_steps.action: Increase only one dimension at a time, such as duration, movement or body area. Work near hips only if explicitly compatible with veterinary advice and current comfort.
sequential_steps.gate: Repeat comfortable participation before advancing; regress or pause if comfort changes.

sequential_steps.action: Gradually introduce the necessary grooming action, then other familiar tools, locations or people one at a time.
sequential_steps.gate: Comfort is maintained in each new context.

plan.progression_regression: Advance based on observed comfortable voluntary responses. Stop contact immediately for freezing, growling, flinching, escape attempts or increased tension; let him leave and review the medical/behavior plan. Do not treat accepting food as proof of comfort.
plan.generalization: Introduce a different tool, helper or location individually at easier criteria; communicate the stop signals to any groomer.
plan.maintenance: Use brief comfortable practice, breaks and voluntary participation before routine grooming.
plan.troubleshooting: If handling remains uncomfortable, do not increase pressure. Return to the veterinary team and seek qualified reward-based behavior support; medically necessary grooming may need a veterinary sedation/handling plan, not more rehearsal.
welfare_safeguards: No restraint, forced prolonged exposure or provocation to test tolerance.
Provide rest, water and an escape route.
Do not prescribe diagnosis, medication or fixed recovery timeline.
plan.design_choices: The stage order and size of each step are practical adjustable examples, not experimentally proven thresholds. Session length and repetitions remain unset until the profile and response are known.
plan.traceability: This preliminary safety plan follows SKILL.md and references/curriculum-contract.md. No verified empirical source registry was supplied or found in the skill directory, so clinical evidence IDs and claim locators remain unresolved.

execution_blockers: No individual health, mobility, bite history, onset, urgent grooming needs, preferred rewards or practical constraints supplied.
No reusable verified general-evidence artifacts supplied; the skill bundle contains contracts but no source registry.
Veterinary assessment is needed before hip-contact training; a remote report cannot establish diagnosis or a safe hands-on procedure.
